title: French far right gets tangled up in headscarf ban proposal
subhead: Intended as a communications coup, the revival of the long-standing debate within the Rassemblement National over banning the headscarf in public spaces has exposed legal uncertainties and disagreements between Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella.

First bodies of Philippines ferry fire victims land as toll rises to 35
subhead: On Saturday morning, tents were being set up to receive the bodies of the passengers who were killed Wednesday in a ferry fire, which had begun in the cargo hold before tearing through the ship 'in seconds.'

title: 'The protection of Paris's iconic zinc rooftops is now putting undue strain on the city's livability'
subhead: The ability to shelter from the heat has become a key component of a home's value. The situation in the French capital – with its top-floor apartments that have become unlivable – is a case in point, writes Dominique Naert, a civil engineering and sustainable building expert.

title: Céline Dion's 'giant karaoke' brings together Paris fans in song
subhead: On the eve of the first in a series of 16 concerts by the Québécois superstar in the French capital, nearly 10,000 people gathered at Place de la Bataille-de-Stalingrad in the 19th arrondissement and shared a communal and euphoric moment.

title: Thomas Piketty: 'To solve today's contradictions, we must rethink prosperity while respecting planetary boundaries'
subhead: Adapting the economy to climate change must go hand in hand with economic democracy, self-management, political and territorial equality and a move away from market-driven approaches, writes economist Thomas Piketty.

The forgotten French prisoner of 9/11
subhead: Zacarias Moussaoui, who was sent to the US by Al-Qaeda to prepare attacks and was convicted of complicity in the September 11 attacks, has spent the past 20 years serving a life sentence without the possibility of parole in a high-security penitentiary in Colorado. His lawyer is requesting his transfer to France.

title: Céline Dion's Paris residency brings economic boost: 'When you're a fan, money is no object'
subhead: After six years away from the stage, the Québécois superstar begins a run of 26 concerts in Paris on Saturday. Hoteliers, restaurateurs and retailers hope to benefit from the influx of nearly 800,000 fans, both French and international. The windfall is estimated at between €500 million and €1 billion, but it comes at a climate cost.

title: 'Al-Qaeda's trap was the long wars that helped bring Trump to power on the promise to end them'
subhead: In an interview, Yves Trotignon, a former French intelligence official, describes how the 2001 attack plunged the West into an era of permanent terrorist threat. He explains that protracted conflicts led to abandoning 'certain forms of the rule of law.'
